plain.li: Nearly there, nearly there.
Gently does it.
[winter] Snow on your back again, look at you.
[winter] Breath like smoke, the pair of us.
[rain] Rain or not, the work still wants doing.
[rain] Shake off over there, not on me.
[night] I can't see a thing out here, so you'll have to stand still for me.
[night] Late for both of us, I know.
[job:milk] Good girl, that's the last of it.
[job:shear] Hold still, this is the tricky bit round the legs.
[job:tame] I'll sit here as long as it takes.
[job:train] Once more, and then a treat.
[job:tend] Let me see that, there's a good animal.
[job:feed] Plenty for everyone, no shoving.
[job:rescue] Easy, easy, I'll have you inside in a moment.
[job:rope] Back to the pen with you, and no stopping for the grass.
[childplay] You can have half my bread if you stay.
[childplay] I'm going to tell you a story and you have to listen.

warm.li: There now, you're safe with me.
You've been so patient with me today.

blunt.li: Come on, I haven't got all day.

cheerful.li: Look at you go, you clever thing!
You're doing so well today, you know that?
Best animal in the colony, and I'll tell anyone who asks.

gloomy.li: You and me, stuck with the dirty jobs again.
Don't look at me like that, I didn't choose this either.
At least one of us is having a good day.

cold.li: No sudden moves, and I'll make none either.

plain.li: Out here it's just chewing and the wind.
I could watch them all afternoon.
[child] That one's the boss, I can tell.
[child] I'm going to count them all, every single one.
[evening] Last light, and every one of them accounted for.
[evening] Listen to them settling, that's the best bit of the day.
[spring] New grass, and they know it.
[spring] Half of them shedding and all of them hungry.
[winter] Frost on their backs, and not one of them minds.
[winter] Thick coats on all of them, good.

warm.li: Every one of them fed and safe.
Shove over, you lot, I've come to sit with you.

cheerful.li: Fat and happy, the lot of them, and not a care between them.
If I had my way, I'd eat my supper out here with them.

gloomy.li: They'll still be grazing here long after the rest of us.
They don't ask how I'm doing, and that suits me.

cold.li: Fodder holding, coats good, nobody limping.

plain.li: Lift your foot, no, the other one.
You've half the field in this coat.
[named] There you are, {OTHER_nameDef}, fit to be seen.
[named] Stand still, {OTHER_nameDef}, you'll thank me later.
[named] Easy, {OTHER_nameDef}, I'm only after the burrs.
[young] All fluff and no patience, aren't you?
[winter] Frozen mud in your coat, let's knock it out.
[winter] Coat as thick as a blanket, I'm almost jealous.
[summer] Flies again, stand still and I'll get the worst of them.
[summer] Too hot for all this hair, let's get some of it off you.
[rain] Mud to your knees, where have you been?
[rain] Wet through, let's get you dry before you take a chill.
[rain] You smell like a wet rug, a lovely wet rug.

warm.li: Take your time, there's no hurry today.

blunt.li: Hold still, I'm not doing this twice.

cheerful.li: Look at that shine, the others will be jealous!
You'll be the smartest beast in the pen by the time I'm done.

gloomy.li: One of us might as well look tidy today.
You don't mind my company, which is more than most do.

cold.li: Stand square, this takes as long as it takes.

plain.li: {PAWN_nameDef} stopped {OTHER_nameDef} to say {PET_nameDef} was resting easy and would be up soon.
{PAWN_nameDef} said {PET_nameDef} had lifted its head and looked round for {OTHER_nameDef} during the rounds.
{PAWN_nameDef} sought out {OTHER_nameDef} to say {PET_nameDef} had had a good day.
[sick] {PAWN_nameDef} told {OTHER_nameDef} that {PET_nameDef} had slept through the night, which was a good sign.
[sick] {PAWN_nameDef} let {OTHER_nameDef} know that {PET_nameDef} had kept its food down at last.
[hurt] {PAWN_nameDef} let {OTHER_nameDef} know that {PET_nameDef} had stopped worrying at the dressing, so it must hurt less.
[hurt] {PAWN_nameDef} was pleased with how {PET_nameDef} was moving today, and said so to {OTHER_nameDef}.

warm.li: {PAWN_nameDef} sat with {OTHER_nameDef} and talked about {PET_nameDef} until {OTHER_nameDef} could smile again.
{PAWN_nameDef} told {OTHER_nameDef} that {PET_nameDef} had been asking for {OTHER_objective}, in its way.

blunt.li: {PAWN_nameDef} said {PET_nameDef} was on the mend and {OTHER_nameDef} could stop hovering.
{PAWN_nameDef} kept it short: {PET_nameDef} would be fine.

cheerful.li: {PAWN_nameDef} told {OTHER_nameDef} that {PET_nameDef} was already back to its old tricks.
{PAWN_nameDef} came to say {PET_nameDef} had tried to steal {PAWN_possessive} lunch, which was a good sign.
{OTHER_nameDef} heard from {PAWN_nameDef} that {PET_nameDef} would be bossing the others again in no time.

gloomy.li: {PAWN_nameDef} told {OTHER_nameDef} that {PET_nameDef} would pull through, though it would take time.
{PAWN_nameDef} warned {OTHER_nameDef} that {PET_nameDef} was still weak, but no worse.
{PAWN_nameDef} asked {OTHER_nameDef} not to expect too much of {PET_nameDef} just yet.

cold.li: {PAWN_nameDef} gave {OTHER_nameDef} {PET_nameDef}'s progress in one plain word: improving.
{PAWN_nameDef} reported to {OTHER_nameDef} that {PET_nameDef} was eating, drinking and recovering.

plain.li: All that training, and here you are.
Let me look at you properly.
[named] There you are, {PET_nameDef}, all grown up.
[named] Steady, {PET_nameDef}, you'll get used to it.
[shiny] Even brighter than before, if that's possible.

warm.li: You've worked so hard for this.
Big or small, you're still my partner.

cheerful.li: Wait until the others see you.

gloomy.li: I'll miss how small you were.
You won't fit in my lap anymore, will you?

cold.li: Evolution complete, now we test it.

plain.li: I've never seen one do that up close.
Is it meant to glow like that?
So that's what all the training was for.
[named] {PET_nameDef} has grown, hasn't it, {OTHER_nameDef}?

warm.li: It's lovely to see it so happy.

cheerful.li: Best thing I've seen all week!
Can I pat it, or is it too grand now?

gloomy.li: It'll eat twice as much now, I suppose.
Hope it still knows who its friends are.

cold.li: A sensible use of training time.

plain.li: [meme:AM_Cowboys] Showed {OTHER_nameDef} how to read a herd from the fence before it moves. Quick to catch on.
[meme:AM_Cowboys] {OTHER_nameDef} asked me about the open range. I talked until the lamp was out and could have gone on.
[!meme:AM_Cowboys] {OTHER_nameDef} counts the herd at dusk, every night, twice. I've started doing it too.
[!meme:AM_Cowboys] Spent the evening at the fence with {OTHER_nameDef}, who talks about grazing the way some people talk about poetry.
Out by the pens with {OTHER_nameDef} until dark, talking about the animals and hardly at all about ourselves.

warm.li: {OTHER_nameDef} and I agreed the herd is family, the loud and smelly part of it.
Good company at the fence tonight. {OTHER_nameDef} knows every animal by its walk.

blunt.li: Talked herds with {OTHER_nameDef}. Knows the work.

cheerful.li: {OTHER_nameDef} and I gave every animal in the pen a new name, again, and argued longest over the bull's.

gloomy.li: Talked about the herd with {OTHER_nameDef}. Easier than talking about anything else.
{OTHER_nameDef} says a good herd outlives its keepers. I'm not sure that's a comfort.

cold.li: Compared notes on the herd with {OTHER_nameDef}. Our counts matched. Our methods did not.
{OTHER_nameDef} has sound views on rotating the grazing. Worth listening to.
